name: isOutboundCertificateValidationEnforced
definition: True when the email service requires TLS and refuses to deliver outbound mail to a receiving server whose TLS certificate is not valid (self-signed, expired or for another name). False when TLS is not required, because mail can then still go out unencrypted.
population: the outbound mail the email service sends for one account; one account-level setting
evidenceRequiredForTrue: A successful read of the account's enforced TLS setting showing TLS is required and a valid certificate is required for delivery; an error, 401/403 or empty read is Not evaluated.
citations: SendGrid API reference, Enforced TLS settings (twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-enforced-tls): GET /v3/user/settings/enforced_tls returns require_tls, require_valid_cert and version

changeLog.change: Registered so the SendGrid email-security transformations can emit it. Meaning written from the public SendGrid API reference and one read of a real account (read-only); no replay-backed validation yet, so the key stays proposed and V0.

notes: Judged together with require_tls, like isOutboundMinimumTLSVersionSecure, because SendGrid applies the certificate setting only under a required-TLS policy; isOutboundTLSEnforced reports require_tls on its own. Read from SendGrid require_tls and require_valid_cert. Messaging Security is allowed too because the SendGrid integration is catalogued under communication (Messaging Security).
